recent_articles.title: Meenakshi Natarajan nomination: Congress leaders eyeing RS seat ‘spoilt’ chances of party nominee, says M.P. CM - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chief Minister Mohan Yadav** of **Madhya Pradesh** accused the **Congress** of deliberately sabotaging **Meenakshi Natarajan's** nomination for a Rajya Sabha seat, alleging that it was part of an attempt to secure the seat themselves.  The nomination was rejected by the Returning Officer based on allegations of undisclosed information in her form, which led to **Mahesh Kewat**, the BJP candidate for the third seat, winning unopposed. The **Congress** has challenged the rejection and plans a statewide protest.

recent_articles.title: Madhya Pradesh Removes Two-Child Norm For Government Employees
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Madhya Pradesh**'s government has reversed its two-child restriction policy for government servants.  Chief Minister Dr Mohan Yadav ordered the removal of the provision from the state's Civil Services Rules, which had barred candidates with more than two living children from government jobs since 2001. The decision aligns the state with Rajasthan and Chhattisgarh, which have also lifted similar restrictions. This move is expected to provide relief for job aspirants and government employees who previously faced this policy.

recent_articles.title: Beyond Religion, Caste, Class: BJP Eyes UP Via Madhya Pradesh Rajya Sabha Seat
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The BJP has nominated **Mahesh Kewat**, chairman of the Madhya Pradesh State Fisherman Welfare Board, to represent the state in the Rajya Sabha. This nomination is being interpreted as a symbolic gesture drawing on the Ramayana story of Lord Ram's boatman, Kewat, who helped him cross the river. The BJP hopes this move will resonate with Extremely Backward Classes communities and strengthen its presence in Bundelkhand, while also sending a morale-boosting message to its cadre.  This strategy could be part of a larger plan for both Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh's upcoming elections.

recent_articles.title: Rare Caracal Spotted In Madhya Pradesh's Kuno National Park After Decades
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A **Caracal**, one of India's rarest wild cats, has been recorded in camera trap footage inside Madhya Pradesh's Kuno National Park after decades. The sighting is being hailed as a positive indicator for the park's ecological health and biodiversity.  **Chief Minister Dr Mohan Yadav** described the event as a major achievement for wildlife conservation efforts in the state, attributing it to Project Cheetah's role in restoring the ecosystem. Wildlife experts view this development as significant because the presence of a top predator like the Caracal often indicates healthy prey populations and a functioning ecosystem.

recent_articles.title: After a gap of 21 years, M.P. government to relaunch State-wide public bus service - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Mohan Yadav**, the Chief Minister of **Madhya Pradesh**, announced the relaunch of a state-wide public transport bus service, 'Mukhya Mantri Sugam Parivahan Sewa', in phases across the state. The service will be launched by the **Madhya Pradesh Passenger Transport and Infrastructure Limited** under a public-private partnership (PPP) model, with operations starting from Indore in July.  The initiative aims to address challenges related to distances between cities and provide convenient travel options for citizens, particularly women.

recent_articles.title: After a gap of 21 years, M.P. government to relaunch State-wide public bus service - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Mohan Yadav**, the Chief Minister of **Madhya Pradesh**, announced the relaunch of a state-wide public transport bus service, 'Mukhya Mantri Sugam Parivahan Sewa', in phases across the state. The service will be launched by the **Madhya Pradesh Passenger Transport and Infrastructure Limited** and is expected to address challenges posed by distances between cities and provide convenient travel options for citizens. The first phase will launch from Indore in July, with services including intracity, intercity, and inter-state routes.  The initiative aims to improve connectivity within the state and neighboring states, addressing concerns about safety and accessibility of public transport.

recent_articles.title: M.P. CM announces financial aid to people died in Bhojshala movement; govt to build Saraswati corridor, research centre - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Mohan Yadav**, Chief Minister of **Madhya Pradesh**, announced financial assistance to the families of three men who died during protests at the Bhojshala temple in 2003.  He also declared the site a temple dedicated to goddess Vagdevi and announced construction of a "Saraswati Lok" corridor and a Raja Bhoj Research Institute. The **Madhya Pradesh High Court** ruled that the site is a temple, dismissing the Muslim community's claim that it was a mosque.

recent_articles.title: Twisha Sharma death case: husband Samarth Singh brought to Bhopal, police to seek remand - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Samarth Singh**, the husband of Twisha Sharma, who was found dead in her marital home on May 12th, 2026, was arrested by **Madhya Pradesh police** after he surrendered at a Jabalpur district court.  He is being held for questioning regarding his alleged involvement in dowry death and harassment. The case has prompted the State government to recommend a Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe into Sharma's death.  The investigation is ongoing, with **Giribala Singh**, former judge and chairperson of the Bhopal Consumer Court, stating she is willing to provide a statement but has not yet been contacted by police.

recent_articles.title: Death toll in explosion at firecracker factory in M.P.'s Dewas rises to five - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Five workers have died after an explosion at a firecracker factory in Madhya Pradesh's Dewas district, with 23 others hospitalized. **Anil Malviya**, the licensed owner of the factory, has been arrested under the National Security Act (NSA) and his license suspended.  **Chief Minister Mohan Yadav** visited the hospital where the injured are being treated, promising a thorough investigation into the incident. The state government is also conducting a magisterial inquiry and has ordered an investigation by officials from the Petroleum and Explosives Safety Organization (PESO), the State Pollution Control Board, and the Forensic Science Laboratory.

recent_articles.title: PM austerity appeal: State leaders take steps to limit their fuel use - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Prime Minister Narendra Modi**, **Union Home Minister Amit Shah**, and several other state chief ministers have implemented measures to reduce fuel consumption in response to the West Asia crisis.  These include reducing convoy sizes, promoting electric vehicles, and encouraging public transport use. **Yogi Adityanath**, **Rekha Gupta**, **Mohan Yadav**, and others have also taken steps to promote sustainability within their respective states.  **Devendra Fadnavis**, **Harsh Sanghavi**, and **Acharya Devvrat** have implemented similar measures in Maharashtra, Gujarat, and Bihar respectively.

recent_articles.title: Two cheetahs released into wild in Kuno; CM Yadav says M.P. now recognised as ‘Cheetah State’ - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Mohan Yadav** released two cheetahs from Botswana into an open forest in Kuno National Park, marking another successful chapter of the **Project Cheetah**.  The reintroduction program aims to restore the endangered species and prepare them for free roaming. This is the third international phase of the project, following previous arrivals from Namibia and South Africa. The release follows a quarantine period and experts believe cheetahs from Botswana will contribute to a healthy and sustainable population in Kuno.

recent_articles.title: West Bengal Cabinet 2026: From Dilip Ghosh to Agnimitra Paul, Ministers who were sworn in along with Suvendu Adhikari - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Suvendu Adhikari**, newly sworn in as the Chief Minister of West Bengal, inducted five new ministers into his cabinet on Saturday. The swearing-in ceremony was attended by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi**, **Union Ministers Amit Shah, Rajnath Singh, J. P. Nadda, and Dharmendra Pradhan**, among other BJP leaders.  **Dilip Ghosh**, a senior BJP leader who secured victory in the Kharagpur seat, **Agnimitra Paul**, a fashion designer-turned-legislator who won Asansol Dakshin, **Ashok Kirtania**, a BJP stalwart who gained victory in Bangaon Uttar, and **Kshudiram Tudu**, a former school teacher from Ranibandh (ST) constituency, were among the newly appointed ministers.  **Nisith Pramanik**, a key face of BJP from North Bengal, was also inducted into the cabinet.

recent_articles.title: M.P. Assembly passes resolution to implement women’s reservation after delimitation amid uproar by Opposition - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Madhya Pradesh** Assembly passed a resolution to implement women's reservation following the delimitation exercise, despite opposition from the Congress.  **Chief Minister Mohan Yadav** proposed the resolution, urging immediate implementation after the completion of the delimitation process. The resolution was met with resistance from the Opposition, who argued that the government's actions contradicted its words and called for an immediate enforcement of the Women's Reservation Act.

recent_articles.title: BJP claiming ‘fake credit’ for raising land acquisition compensation for farmers; law made by UPA govt, says Congress - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Congress party** alleged that the **Madhya Pradesh** government was falsely claiming credit for doubling land acquisition compensation, a provision enacted by the **UPA government** under former Prime Minister **Manmohan Singh** in 2013. The state cabinet approved an increase to double the market price of land acquired for farmers, with Chief Minister **Mohan Yadav** calling it a "major decision in the interest of farmers."

recent_articles.title: M.P. farmers to get four times the market price compensation for agricultural land accusation, says CM Yadav - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Madhya Pradesh**'s Cabinet increased compensation for agricultural land acquisition to four times the market price, effective immediately. Chief Minister **Mohan Yadav** announced the decision at a press conference in Bhopal, stating it would benefit farmers and expedite infrastructure projects like irrigation schemes, roads, bridges, railway lines, and dams.  The cost of these projects will not be reduced despite the compensation increase.
